## Summary
Instrument the game so a run emits telemetry: per-tick state plus discrete events, tagged with the run seed and schema version. Must cover both human play and the bot, and must not affect gameplay.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Each tick records a compact state vector (player pos/vel/heading, hold/levels, enemies, enemy bullets, drops, minerals, boss) reusing the existing `BotSnapshot` builder where possible.
- AC2: The human/bot input for the tick is recorded alongside the state (the input actually applied).
- AC3: Discrete events are recorded: run start (seed), deaths/hits, pickups, hold-full choice + selection, wave/level transitions, boss phase, run end (win/lose).
- AC4: Recording works when the bot drives and when a human drives, in `PlayScene`; shared-core scenes can opt in.
- AC5: Overhead is bounded and gameplay is unchanged (regression tests); telemetry off = zero records.
- AC6: Unit tests for the state/event serialisation and seed/version tagging.
data.title: Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state and events

data.description:
## Summary
Dev tooling to record a human session, analyse it offline and replay/ghost it against the bot — the data loop for tuning and evaluating the bot.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A dev command/mode records a human session to JSONL (state + input + events + seed) using the telemetry framework.
- AC2: An offline analysis script produces a report: key-hold duration histogram, input-change cadence, reaction latency proxy, target-choice stats (mineral/power-up/enemy), engagement distances, dodge outcomes, survival/minerals-per-minute.
- AC3: A replay/ghost viewer steps a recording deterministically and overlays human vs bot input/position (same seed).
- AC4: The recorded dataset is versioned and documented so scripts can evolve with the schema.
- AC5: Tests for the analyser (pure stats) and the replay stepping.
- AC6: Docs: how to record, analyse and replay.
data.title: Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling

data.description:
## Summary
Replace the per-frame priority ladder with a **bot framework**: a world model, a registry of goals/behaviours, a committed policy and a content configuration seam. This is the maintainable core that later content and styles plug into.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A `BotBrain`/policy interface that maps a `BotSnapshot` (+ world model + memory) to an input, with an explicit **commitment** mechanism (a selected goal is held until achieved, invalidated, or outranked by a margin for a minimum time).
- AC2: A **goal/behaviour registry**: goals and behaviours register by id; adding one does not require editing the core switch/if-chain.
- AC3: A world-model/predictor layer (positions/velocities, incoming-fire prediction) separated from decision policy, so prediction is testable in isolation.
- AC4: The existing pure `decideBotInput` is preserved behind an adapter (so current tests/gyms keep working) or cleanly superseded with documented parity tests.
- AC5: The framework is deterministic and pure over an injected `dt`/clock; no wall-clock dependence.
- AC6: Unit tests: registry, commitment/hysteresis, deterministic replay of a decision sequence.
- AC7: Docs: framework overview + how goals/behaviours are structured.
data.title: Bot framework core: world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy

data.description:
## Summary
Turn on telemetry in **production** for playtesters: an explicit opt-in consent flow, privacy-safe records, batched upload to a remote sink, and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: An in-game consent/opt-in prompt (and a settings toggle) gating production telemetry; default **off**; easy opt-out.
- AC2: A remote sink that batches and uploads records (endpoint configurable), with retry/backoff and no gameplay impact when offline.
- AC3: Records are PII-free and documented; a data-retention/privacy note is included in the docs and (if applicable) the consent screen.
- AC4: A remote-off/no-op path so local dev and offline play are unaffected (tests).
- AC5: A simple way to inspect downloaded telemetry (reuse the analysis tooling from child 4).
- AC6: Tests for consent gating, the uploader's batching/backoff, and the disabled path.
- AC7: Docs: telemetry privacy + how playtester data is stored and used.
data.title: Production telemetry: opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink

data.description:
# Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the Central AI boss to require 200 hits total (readable as 4 phases of 50) and I want its health bar pinned to the top of the screen so I can always read my progress regardless of where the boss is.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC1 and AC4.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` and `_totalHp = BOSS_PHASE_COUNT * BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` (400 total). Doc comment and `BossConfig.initialHp` comment reference 400/100.
- `healthBarGraphics` is created with `scene.add.graphics()`, then `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` puts it in the boss **container**, so it renders offset by the boss position even though `_drawHealthBar()` uses screen coordinates and `setScrollFactor(0)`.
- `getHpFraction()` is already proportional and the four phase-segment dividers already exist — keep both.

## Desired change

1. Change `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` to `50`; total becomes **200**. Update every comment/constant reference from 100/400 to 50/200 (including `BossConfig.initialHp` docs).
2. Remove the `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` container membership so the bar is a **scene child** (it is already created via `scene.add.graphics()`); keep `setScrollFactor(0)` and `setDepth(100)`. It now renders at the absolute screen coordinates drawn by `_drawHealthBar()` (horizontally centred at `BOSS_HEALTH_BAR_Y`).
3. Keep the proportional fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
4. Ensure `destroy()` still explicitly destroys `healthBarGraphics`.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — HP constants/comments, health-bar re-parenting.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — health-model and health-bar placement tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym health-bar placement expectations.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — health-bar layering assumptions if any.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE === 50` and total HP is 200; hitting 49 times keeps phase 1, the 50th hit advances to phase 2, and the 200th hit destroys the boss.
- The health bar Graphics is **not** a child of the boss container and its screen position is unchanged when the boss position changes (assert `boss.x`/`boss.y` separately from the bar's drawn position).
- `getHpFraction()` decreases monotonically with each hit from 1.0 toward 0.
- The four phase-segment dividers and the proportional fill are retained.
- All `Boss.test.ts` / `GymBoss.test.ts` assertions updated for 200 HP pass.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC1) **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
- (parent AC4) **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
data.title: Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar
